topic: Peptides your body makes: CCK (cholecystokinin), the gut's own 'I'm full' signal. Made by I cells (enteroendocrine cells) mainly in the duodenum and jejunum; released by fats, proteins and amino acids (glucose only briefly); blood levels rise from 0.5-1 pM to 5-15 pM within minutes of eating (Chandra & Liddle, Pancreapedia 2018); Ivy & Oldberg 1928 (Am J Physiol 86:599): intestinal extracts made the gallbladder contract, hence the name; also stimulates pancreatic enzyme secretion (once called pancreozymin, Harper & Raper 1943) and delays gastric emptying; acts on CCK1 receptors on vagal afferent nerves that signal the hindbrain to limit intake; first hormone shown to cause satiety: Gibbs, Young & Smith 1973 in rats (SSIB Ingestive Classics); CCK-8 infusion decreased food intake in humans (Kissileff et al., Am J Clin Nutr 1981)

cards.html:
Order #CCKYour gut
Body-made peptide

Your gut makes its own “I'm full” signal.

Item 01Who

Meet CCK

Short for cholecystokinin. A small peptide hormone.

Made by I cells in your upper small intestine.

Item 02Trigger

Fat + protein arrive

Food moves from stomach to small intestine.

Blood CCK rises within minutes.

Item 03Found

1928

Gut extracts made the gallbladder squeeze. The name comes from that job.

Item 04Its jobs
1Squeezes the gallbladder: bile helps digest fat
2Tells the pancreas to send enzymes
3Slows stomach emptying

Item 05Fullness

“Enough”

CCK acts on the vagus nerve, which signals your brainstem.

Result: smaller meals. Rats 1973. People 1981.

TotalThank you

Ghrelin

says “eat”

CCK

says “enough”
